Two limits of the model review are recorded so it is not mistaken for authority: its evidence check called the guard unit unverified although X08/logs/14 reports `ℹ tests 5 / pass 5 / fail 0`, and its reference to 'issue #621' is not reproducible from the repository (it had no network tools), so nothing was built on it.

Method caveat, cost again: full 40-hex shas come from tool output or are re-derived by the generator, never from memory. While emitting X09 the generator was handed a93b53a075a1d542...; the real parent of 147b8271 is a93b53a076ca136d0871250d475577f9d574d86d. The generator's `git rev-parse HEAD^ == baseSha` guard threw, so no record was written with the invented sha. Abbreviations are harmless in prose; a wrong full sha in a record poisons chain continuity silently.

Citation defect found by this unit, corrected rather than hidden: PLAN-COMPLETION.json and the X09 record's note text cited 'X08/logs/20' for the branch-only failure attribution. No such log exists -- X08/logs ends at 19. The attribution it was cited for is produced in X09/logs/04 and X10/logs/01, from commands re-run at 147b8271, at origin/main 1bd754cf/b0c0e75d and at the merge commit. A citation that points at a file nobody wrote is as bad as a dangling evidence path; the series' scanner checks the latter and had no rule for the former.

Lesson recorded twice now and finally acted on (E03->E04, then X10): a branch must be measured against the current integration tip. X08/X09 were scored against a main 13 commits stale, which manufactured ten 'regressions' that were main's own missing fixes (runtime-isolation-stress, artifacts-paging, git-remote-ref, herdr-forks, platform-filelock-no-hardlinks, runtime-isolation-registry, safe-git-survivors, safe-git-units, standalone-plan-flow, worktree-janitor -- all green alone once origin/main was merged in, 195 tests / 195 pass, X10/logs/01). Measuring alone, one process per file, at three trees is what distinguishes a stale base from a regression; `git diff --name-only <main>...HEAD` intersected with the failing file list settles it in one command.

Platform finding, not branch debt: test/integration/worker-budget-build-hint.test.ts (main's own, c379a805 / PR #610) can hold `npm test` open forever. Its stub worker resolves only on `req.signal` abort, the budget is 1000 ms, node's default per-test timeout is Infinity, and under load average 82 copies on both this tree and main's tree hit a 240 s wall while an interleaved round at load 25.86 saw main fail its own hint assertion in 2 of 4 copies as the merged tree passed 8 of 8 (X10/logs/05). The series' suite-termination requirement is met at this tree; the exposure lives in main's test design and needs a per-test timeout or a watchdog that cannot be starved.

Lint parity gap, measured and left open for the operator: origin/main is clean under `biome check src cmd` (0 findings) and this branch is not (47 findings in 15 files, all written by earlier units of this series; whole-tree `biome check .` reports 513 errors against main's 2). Earlier units each ran biome only over the files they touched, so the tree-wide debt accumulated invisibly across ~100 commits. The mechanical fix is not mechanical: `biome check --write` over the 15 files rewrote 37 files (+2855/-591) and still left 13 flagged with 45 findings requiring --unsafe; it was reverted and recorded (X10/logs/04) rather than folded into a behaviour PR.

Convention conflict inside the series, recorded rather than silently resolved: .gitignore (Bootstrap Protocol 2026-11-03) says per-unit logs, fixtures and handoffs 'must stay untracked; integrity comes from handoffHash + artifactSha256', and the gate does stamp only a clean worktree -- but every unit from X01 on has force-added its evidence so a reviewer can open the paths a record cites, and the integrity scanner counts a cited-but-untracked path as dangling (evidence untracked=0 is only reachable by committing them). X10 follows the series' actual practice (force-add) and flags the rule as the thing that should change, not the practice.

X11 corrected a cause claim X10's committed record makes. X10's notes and logs attribute X08/out's 8-character resultSha to `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` under GIT_COMMON_DIR. That is not how it was written: X08's generator carried it as a literal (`resultSha: "9f064450",`), and the durable facts are that templates/handoff.schema.json types baseSha/resultSha as plain {"type":"string"} -- so the emit path had nothing to check it against -- and that the stored value is byte-identical to `git rev-parse --short 9f0644507e51baea9f6d0a75fc838e046c4143b7`. X10/out is hash-bound and keeps the wrong cause; the correction lives in X10/out-chain and X11/logs/01.

The writer can still produce the defect X11 declares. templates/handoff.schema.json still types baseSha and resultSha as plain {"type":"string"} and nextBaseSha as {"type":["string","null"]} -- no pattern, no length -- so writeHandoff accepts any shape, hashes it into handoffHash, and commits it. The chain gate now catches and names it on every run and X11 declares the only instance the series produced with a proved-unique referent, but the durable fix is a shape pattern on those three fields, which changes the handoff protocol for every record in the series: the operator's call, not an audit-tooling unit's. Unchanged from X10 and still open: worker-budget-build-hint.test.ts hangs under concurrency on this branch (green alone, green at origin/main), and `biome check src cmd` is red with 44 findings across 14 files this branch wrote (green at origin/main).

Every X-series suite tally before X12 was taken with `npx tsx --test` and no preload.

`npm run lint` (= `biome check .`, the repository's gate) is exit 1 at the branch tip with 516 findings over 488 files, against exit 0 at origin/main tip e7888752. 365 are the evidence tree (json), whose bytes are hash-bound (evidence[].sha256, stdoutSha256, handoffHash) and which AUDIT/integrity-scan.mjs checks only for existence and tracked-ness, so formatting them would make the trail unverifiable silently; 118 ts + 5 mjs are code this branch wrote (~500 formatter findings + 15 analyzer errors, fixable). Merging as-is takes main from exit 0 to exit 1. Options and the biome.json golden-file precedent: X12/logs/06.

Whole suite at the branch tip under the gate invocation: 7964 tests / 7956 pass / 3 fail / 0 cancelled in 15m26s (X12/logs/02). The three failing leaves reproduce identically at origin/main's tip in a separate checkout (X12/logs/02-three-leaves-at-origin-main-e7888752.txt): they are pre-existing on main, not branch damage. X12's record does not list the whole-suite run in `commands[]` -- resultGate requires proof exitCode 0 (src/bootstrap/resultGate.ts:33) -- it is carried as evidence instead of being made to look green.
